newsitem.title: UK: U.S. planes attack rural targets in Iraq - Britain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. planes attack rural targets in Iraq - Britain.

text.p: Defence Secretary Michael Portillo told BBC radio on Tuesday no British planes were involved in the U.S. air raid on Iraq but Britain had lent logistical support.
"This operation did not involve British attack aircraft. We were asked and granted logistics suppport to the Americans," Portillo said.
He said U.S. planes had attacked rural targets in Iraq.

"The Americans have launched a number of military attacks against rural areas. They are purely military targets. They have been selected to minimise collateral damage, that is to say loss of civilian life," Portillo said in an interview.

"The no-fly zone in southern Iraq will be extended to allow the allies operating there to have a greater opportunity to control more of Saddam's airspace and bring greater control over him," he added.
Portillo was speaking minutes after the Pentagon announced the U.S. attack. He did not give details but said only U.S. forces were involved.
